docs.title: MedVol
docs.text:
Faithful N:N conversion of medical image formats through one neutral model: the MLArray v1 metadata model. Formats: NIfTI-1/2, NRRD, MetaImage, MGH/MGZ, DICOM (single-frame and enhanced multi-frame series, SEG) and .mla.

Documentation: mic-dkfz.github.io/MedVol. Design: docs/design/spec.md.

docs.title: Guarantees
docs.text:
• Faithful round trips. X → .mla → X reproduces the array bit-identically and the header to the accuracy of the format (identical binary floats, identical numeric values for text formats).
  • Nothing implicit. No reorientation, resampling, rescaling or dtype change, and no metadata removal. The array keeps its stored values and order; scaling becomes values.scale/offset.
  • Exact geometry. MedVol computes geometry from the format's own fields (backends do byte-level IO only). Every voxel keeps its world position across formats, including oblique, mirrored and gantry-tilted (sheared) grids.
  • Everything reported. Each read, write and convert returns a report of choices, warnings and dropped fields; it is also stored in the image's history.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
import medvol

image, report = medvol.read("ct.nii.gz")              # Image(array, mlarray Meta) + Report
print(report)
medvol.write(image, "ct.mla")
medvol.convert("dicom_dir/", "ct.mla", dicom_tilt="exact")
medvol.convert("ct.mla", "out_dir/", target_format="dicom")   # re-emits the original series
print(medvol.inspect("scan.nrrd"))

medvol convert ct.nii.gz ct.mla --nifti-form sform
medvol inspect dicom_dir/

Ambiguities are resolved by explicit policies (medvol.Policy), for example nifti_form when qform and sform disagree, world_frame (dicom_patient = LPS by default, or ras), dicom_stacks, dicom_tilt, dicom_irregular_spacing and on_loss (warn or error when the target cannot represent something).

The original header is kept, readable, in image.meta.source, and is used again only when writing the same format.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
pip install medvol            # NIfTI, NRRD, MetaImage, MGH/MGZ, .mla
pip install "medvol[dicom]"   # plus DICOM (pydicom, highdicom)

Plugins for further formats can be added through the medvol.formats entry point group.

docs.title: CLI
docs.text: Installing MedVol adds the medvol command.

docs.title: medvol convert
docs.text:
Convert a file or DICOM directory and print the report.

medvol convert ct.nii.gz ct.mla
medvol convert dicom_dir/ ct.nii.gz --dicom-stacks largest --world-frame ras
medvol convert ct.mla ct.mha --on-loss error          # fail instead of dropping what MetaImage cannot store
medvol convert ct.mla out_dir/ --target-format dicom  # re-emit the original DICOM series
option meaning --source-format NAME input format, if it cannot be detected --target-format NAME output format, if the extension does not say (e.g. dicom) --nifti-form, --nifti-form-disagreement, --nifti-form-tolerance-mm, --nifti-no-codes NIfTI policies --reorient, --world-frame orientation --dicom-tilt, --dicom-irregular-spacing, --dicom-stacks, --dicom-rescale DICOM policies --vector-frame vector frame --on-loss, --layout writing

Writing a DICOM SEG needs the referenced series and is done from Python (Usage).

docs.title: medvol inspect
docs.text:
Print a summary of a file or DICOM directory in the MLArray vocabulary: shape, dtype, values, axes, spaces and warnings. It takes --format and the same policy options.

medvol inspect ct.nii.gz

ct.nii.gz: nifti, 1 image(s)
[0] shape (7, 6, 5) int32, values measurement
    axes: z:space, y:space, x:space
    space patient: spacing (0.5, 1.0, 2.0), origin (12.5, -30.25, 47.0), letters RIP

docs.title: Formats
docs.text:
format extensions backend reads writes NIfTI-1 / NIfTI-2 .nii, .nii.gz, .hdr/.img (also gzipped) nibabel (header parsing and data IO only) yes yes NRRD .nrrd, .nhdr + data file pynrrd (parsing and data IO only) yes yes MetaImage .mha, .mhd + raw file MedVol's own parser yes yes MGH / MGZ .mgh, .mgz nibabel yes yes DICOM directories, .dcm pydicom, highdicom (pip install "medvol[dicom]") series, enhanced multi-frame, SEG, RTSTRUCT original series, enhanced files, SEG MLArray .mla mlarray yes yes

medvol formats lists the installed plugins, including those of other packages (Writing a plugin).

Backends are used for byte-level IO. MedVol computes the geometry itself from the format's raw header fields, because libraries disagree on several of them (the cases are named below).

docs.title: Capabilities
docs.text:
Each writer declares what it can store. Before writing, MedVol compares the image with these capabilities. What the format cannot store is reported as dropped (on_loss="warn", default) or raises LossError (on_loss="error"). Dimensions, axis types and dtypes the format cannot hold always raise.

NIfTI NRRD MetaImage MGH/MGZ DICOM .mla space axes 1-3 0-3 1-3 3 2-3 any array axes (max) 7 16 11 4 4 32 non-space axes time, channel, component, other time, channel, component, other time, channel, component, other time, channel, component, other time, channel, other all oblique grids yes yes yes yes yes yes sheared grids yes (sform) yes no (closest orthonormal direction, reported) yes yes (tilted series) yes label table no no no no yes (SEG) yes arbitrary metadata (user, profiles) no no no no no yes dtypes int8-64, uint8-64, float32/64, complex64/128 int8-64, uint8-64, float32/64 int8-64, uint8-64, float32/64 uint8, int16, uint16, int32, float32 any any

docs.title: NIfTI-1 / NIfTI-2
docs.text:
• MedVol chooses between qform and sform itself (nifti_form); readers disagree by up to tens of mm when the two differ. Files without codes are an error by default (nifti_no_codes).
  • On write, both forms are regenerated from the core and the original codes are kept while the geometry is unchanged. nibabel's affine/header synchronisation is bypassed, because it rewrites qform, sform and codes on save. For a sheared grid, the sform is exact and the qform is the closest rigid approximation (reported).
  • scl_slope/scl_inter become values.scale/offset; the array keeps the stored values.
  • Extensions are kept verbatim, binary included.
  • Time uses pixdim[4] and xyzt_units; vector intents become a component axis with an explicit vector_frame.
  • NIfTI-2 is supported.

docs.title: NRRD
docs.text:
• MedVol interprets space itself; pynrrd is only used with its default index_order='F'.
  • All 3-D and 4-D spaces are supported, including left-anterior-superior. scanner-xyz and 3D-right-handed/3D-left-handed are read as LPS (as ITK and Slicer do), with a warning. A space dimension without space becomes a non-patient space named nrrd.
  • measurement frame is kept and applied to vector components explicitly.
  • kinds, centerings, custom key-value pairs and comments are kept verbatim. Non-world axes sampled with spacings/axis mins/axis maxs get their start and step at voxel centres, following centerings (cell when absent, as in NRRD and ITK).
  • Time series from NIfTI are written in left-posterior-superior-time space, the 4-D space ITK reads correctly.

docs.title: MetaImage
docs.text:
• TransformMatrix is column-major, one axis per triple. Origin wins over Offset and Position, as in ITK.
  • AnatomicalOrientation is kept verbatim but never used for geometry: ITK writes it in "comes from" convention and never reads it.
  • MetaImage stores orthonormal directions only: a sheared grid is written with the closest orthonormal direction, and this is reported.

docs.title: MGH / MGZ
docs.text:
• goodRASFlag <= 0 is read as FreeSurfer does (coronal LIA, 1 mm); nibabel reads it differently.
  • c_ras is the centre at index N/2, as FreeSurfer defines it.

docs.title: DICOM
docs.text:
Reading:

  1. group by SeriesInstanceUID, then by geometry (orientation, size, spacing), per dicom_stacks;
  2. sort slices by the projection of ImagePositionPatient on the slice normal, never by InstanceNumber;

  3. check spacing regularity (dicom_irregular_spacing) and gantry tilt (dicom_tilt).

  4. Enhanced multi-frame files (also 4-D) use the per-frame functional groups, where some vendors put geometry per frame.

  5. DICOM SEG becomes a label map with codes in values.labels; frames are placed by position, not by order. Fractional SEG becomes values.kind: probability.
  6. RTSTRUCT contours are rasterised onto the referenced series.
  7. The complete header, private tags included, goes to source.header (shared, per_file, file_names).
  8. Siemens mosaic is not supported (it needs a dcm2niix backend).

Writing:

  • Same series: the original files are re-emitted from source, with the original UIDs. Pixel data comes from the array, in the original transfer syntax when it is lossless, otherwise explicit VR little endian (reported). If the data or geometry changed, the data-dependent elements are dropped and new SOP Instance UIDs are generated.
  • New DICOM: only DICOM SEG, from a label map and its referenced series (Usage). New image series from other formats are not created.

docs.title: MLArray (.mla)
docs.text: Read and written by mlarray; nothing is converted. .mla stores everything MedVol reads, including the original header in source, so X → .mla → X is lossless.

docs.title: Geometry and metadata
docs.text:
MedVol's guarantees:

  • Faithful round trips. X → .mla → X reproduces the array bit-identically and the header to the accuracy of the format.
  • Exact geometry. Every voxel keeps its world position across formats, within the format's precision, including oblique, mirrored and gantry-tilted (sheared) grids.
  • Nothing implicit. No reorientation, resampling, rescaling, dtype change or metadata removal unless a policy asks for it. MedVol does not de-identify.
  • Everything reported. See Reports.

These are tested with a conformance phantom: an oblique, mirrored volume in which every voxel encodes its own file index, written with the reference libraries and read and written through every reader × writer pair. World positions must agree to < 1e-4 mm.

docs.title: Array order
docs.text: The array keeps the stored order of the file, in C order: the format's fastest-varying axis is last. A NIfTI, NRRD or MetaImage volume indexed [i, j, k] in the file is array[k, j, i], and DICOM slices are array[slice, row, column]. Axis names (z, y, x, t, ...) are names only; they say nothing about anatomy. source[].index_map records how array axes relate to the file's own index order.

docs.title: Spaces
docs.text:
The geometry is the MLArray space patient (image.space()):

  • its axes are the patient directions: x, y, z increase toward left, posterior, superior (LPS, world_frame="dicom_patient", default) or right, anterior, superior (world_frame="ras");
  • space.from_array.matrix maps array indices of the axes in space.from_array.array_axes to millimetres, with index = voxel centre;
  • non-space axes (time, channel, vector component) never enter the matrix.

Readers build the matrix from the format's own fields (NIfTI qform/sform, NRRD space directions and space origin, MetaImage TransformMatrix/Offset, MGH Mdc/c_ras, DICOM ImagePositionPatient and ImageOrientationPatient). Values are never rounded. Going between LPS and RAS changes the signs of matrix rows; it never flips the array.

space = image.space()
space.matrix()            # (n+1) x (n+1), columns in space.from_array.array_axes order
space.letter_codes()      # e.g. ('R', 'I', 'P'): the direction each mapped axis points to

medvol.reorient(image, "LPS" | "RAS") changes the array order instead, losslessly (Policies).

docs.title: Values
docs.text: The array holds the stored values. Scaling (NIfTI scl_slope/scl_inter, DICOM RescaleSlope/Intercept) goes to values.scale and values.offset: physical value = stored × scale + offset. Label maps from DICOM SEG and RTSTRUCT have values.kind == "label" and a label table with names, colours and codes.

docs.title: Original headers
docs.text:
Every reader stores the complete original header, readable, in image.meta.source (one entry per input):

entry = image.meta.source[0]
entry.format, entry.files          # "nifti", ["ct.nii.gz"]
entry.header["descrip"]            # any header field; DICOM: entry.header["shared"] / ["per_file"]
entry.fingerprint                  # hashes of shape, dtype, geometry and data at read time

When an image is written to the same format, each header field is handled by its class:

class on write examples core-owned regenerated from the MLArray core NIfTI dim, pixdim, qform/sform, datatype, scl_*; NRRD sizes, space directions, kinds; DICOM Rows, PixelSpacing, ImagePositionPatient, RescaleSlope data-dependent kept while the fingerprint still matches the array and geometry; otherwise recomputed or dropped (reported) NIfTI cal_min/cal_max; NRRD min/max; DICOM SmallestImagePixelValue, SliceLocation, SOPInstanceUID verbatim written back as stored descriptions, vendor and acquisition fields, private tags, NRRD custom keys, NIfTI extensions

When writing a different format, only the core is converted. Header fields of one format are never copied into another format's custom keys; the report says so.

docs.title: Writing a plugin
docs.text:
A format is a subclass of FormatPlugin with a reader and a writer that translate between the file and an Image. MedVol does the rest: format detection, policies, capability checks, reorientation, history and reports.

from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
from mlarray import Meta

import medvol
from medvol.plugins.base import Capabilities, FormatPlugin
from medvol.report import Report


class NpyPlugin(FormatPlugin):
    """A bare NumPy array: no geometry, no metadata."""

    name = "npy"
    extensions = (".npy",)
    capabilities = Capabilities(max_space_axes=3, min_space_axes=0, oblique=False, shear=False)

    def sniff(self, path):
        path = Path(path)
        if not path.is_file():
            return 0.0
        with open(path, "rb") as file:
            return 1.0 if file.read(6) == b"\x93NUMPY" else 0.0

    def read(self, path, policy, **options):
        array = np.load(path)
        meta = Meta(axes=[f"axis_{n}" for n in range(array.ndim)], shape=array.shape,
                    source=[{"format": self.name, "files": [Path(path).name]}])
        return [medvol.Image(array, meta)], Report("read", self.name, str(path))

    def write(self, image, path, policy, **options):
        report = Report("write", self.name, str(path))
        if image.meta.spaces:
            report.drop("spaces", "the format has no geometry", policy.on_loss)
        np.save(path, image.array)
        return report


medvol.registry.register(NpyPlugin())
medvol.convert("ct.nii.gz", "ct.npy")        # reports the dropped geometry
image, report = medvol.read("ct.npy")

Guidelines, which the built-in plugins follow:

  • Read the stored values in the stored order (C order, fastest file axis last) and describe them with axes, spaces and values. Record the file's index order in source[].index_map.
  • Compute geometry yourself from the raw header fields, with index = voxel centre, and build patient spaces with medvol.geometry.patient_space(matrix_lps, array_axes, policy.world_frame).
  • Keep the complete header in source[].header, readable, and use it only when writing the same format. Classify its fields with a FieldTable: core-owned fields are regenerated from the core, data-dependent fields are kept only while source[].fingerprint matches.
  • Declare capabilities honestly; MedVol drops or refuses what they exclude before write is called. Anything else you cannot write: report.drop(...) with policy.on_loss.
  • Report every choice with report.choose(name, value) and every doubt with report.warn(message).

docs.title: Registering through an entry point
docs.text:
A package registers its plugins in the medvol.formats entry point group, so they are found when MedVol is imported:

[project.entry-points."medvol.formats"]
npy = "my_package.npy_plugin:NpyPlugin"

A built-in plugin of the same name takes precedence. medvol.registry.register(plugin) replaces any plugin at runtime.

docs.title: Policies
docs.text:
MedVol does nothing implicitly: no reorientation, resampling, rescaling or dtype change, and no metadata removal. Where a file can be read in more than one way, a named policy decides, and the choice is written to the report and to the image's history.

Policies are keyword arguments of read, read_all, write, convert and inspect, fields of medvol.Policy, and flags of the CLI (nifti_form → --nifti-form). The first option is the default.

policy options applies to nifti_form nibabel, sform, qform, itk reading NIfTI nifti_form_disagreement warn, error, ignore reading NIfTI nifti_form_tolerance_mm a distance in mm (default 0.001) reading NIfTI nifti_no_codes error, spec, nibabel, itk reading NIfTI reorient none, LPS, RAS reading world_frame dicom_patient, ras reading dicom_tilt exact, resample, error reading DICOM dicom_irregular_spacing error, split, resample reading DICOM dicom_stacks split, largest, error reading DICOM dicom_rescale error, apply reading DICOM vector_frame from_file, lps, ras, error vector images on_loss warn, error writing layout source, default writing

docs.title: NIfTI
docs.text:
nifti_form: which of the two NIfTI geometries is used. Readers disagree when qform and sform differ (by up to tens of mm in real files), so MedVol makes the choice explicit:

  • nibabel: the sform if sform_code > 0, else the qform;
  • sform / qform: that form;
  • itk: what ITK does.

nifti_form_disagreement: what happens when qform and sform both exist and differ by more than nifti_form_tolerance_mm at the image corners: a warning, an error, or nothing.

nifti_no_codes: a file with qform_code = sform_code = 0 has no defined geometry and tools give three different answers. error refuses it; spec uses the standard's fallback (RAS, diag(pixdim)); nibabel and itk copy those libraries.

docs.title: Orientation and world frame
docs.text:
reorient: none keeps the stored array order. LPS and RAS transpose and flip the array (never resample) so its space axes, fastest first, point closest to x, y, z of that frame. World positions do not change. Also available as medvol.reorient(image, "RAS").

world_frame: the frame of the patient space MedVol builds: dicom_patient (LPS, as DICOM and ITK) or ras (as NIfTI and nibabel). Changing it changes the signs of matrix rows, never the array.

docs.title: DICOM
docs.text:
dicom_tilt: gantry-tilted series have slices that are not perpendicular to the slice direction. exact stores the true, sheared matrix (every voxel at its true position); resample resamples to an orthogonal grid; error refuses. ITK-based readers place tilted slices wrong by tens of mm.

dicom_irregular_spacing: slices with uneven gaps raise (error), are split into regular stacks (split), or are resampled (resample).

dicom_stacks: a series with several geometries (e.g. localizers) is split into one image per stack (split, use read_all), reduced to the largest stack (largest), or refused (error).

dicom_rescale: when RescaleSlope/Intercept differ per slice (common in PET), they cannot be one values.scale/offset. error refuses; apply stores the physical values as float. Written back to DICOM, the stored values are recomputed per slice and must reproduce the array exactly.

docs.title: Vectors
docs.text: vector_frame: the frame vector components (displacement fields, gradients) are expressed in. from_file uses what the file says (NRRD measurement frame, NIfTI intent) and otherwise fails; lps / ras state it. ITK writes LPS and NiftyReg RAS under the same NIfTI intent, so a guess would be wrong half the time.

docs.title: Writing
docs.text:
on_loss: what happens when the target format cannot store something (a sheared grid in MetaImage, user metadata in NIfTI, ...): warn drops it and reports it, error raises LossError. Dimensions, axis types and dtypes the format cannot hold always raise.

layout: the output encoding. source reuses the original encoding, compression and transfer syntax when writing the same format; default uses the writer's default. It never changes which header fields are kept.

docs.title: Reports
docs.text:
read, read_all, write and convert return a Report of everything they decided:

  • choices: what a policy or the data decided (nifti_form = sform (code 1), geometry = reused from source (unchanged), ...);
  • warnings: things that are probably fine but worth knowing (qform and sform disagree, a header of another format is not written, ...);
  • dropped: what the target format cannot store and was left out.
image.meta.user = {"study": "A"}
report = medvol.write(image, "out.nii.gz")
print(report)

write nifti out.nii.gz
  choice: geometry = reused from source (unchanged)
  dropped: user: the format has no place for arbitrary metadata

With on_loss="error", a drop raises medvol.LossError instead, before anything is written:

try:
    medvol.write(image, "out.nii.gz", on_loss="error")
except medvol.LossError as error:
    print(error)            # user: the format has no place for arbitrary metadata

Reading also appends the report to the image's history (action: converted, the tool and version, the choices as settings, warnings and drops as warnings), so a .mla file records how it was made:

image.meta.history[-1]
# {'action': 'converted', 'tool': 'medvol 1.0.0', 'from': 'nifti',
#  'settings': {'nifti_form': 'sform (code 1)'}, 'time': '2026-11-06T12:29:50Z'}

The CLI prints the report of every conversion.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
MedVol reads a file into an Image: the stored array plus its metadata in the MLArray v1 model. Every writer takes that same Image, so any reader can be combined with any writer.

pip install medvol            # NIfTI, NRRD, MetaImage, MGH/MGZ, .mla
pip install "medvol[dicom]"   # plus DICOM (pydicom, highdicom)

docs.title: Read
docs.text:
import medvol

image, report = medvol.read("ct.nii.gz")
print(report)

read nifti ct.nii.gz
  choice: nifti_form = sform (code 1)

image.array is a NumPy array with the stored values, in the stored dtype and the stored order: C order with the format's fastest-varying axis last, so a NIfTI volume [i, j, k] becomes array[k, j, i]. image.meta is an mlarray.Meta:

image.meta.axes                      # z, y, x: names of the array axes, in array order
space = image.space()                # the first space, here "patient" (DICOM patient frame, LPS, mm)
space.matrix()                       # 4x4 from-array matrix; columns follow space.from_array.array_axes
space.spacing, space.origin          # per from_array axis (here x, y, z = NIfTI i, j, k)
space.letter_codes()                 # ('R', 'I', 'P'): where each from_array axis points
image.meta.values                    # kind (measurement, label, ...), unit, scale/offset, labels
image.meta.source[0].header          # the complete original header, readable
image.meta.history                   # one entry per read/convert, with the report's choices

The format is detected from the file content. Pass format="nrrd" (or "dicom", ...) if it cannot be.

docs.title: Several images in one input
docs.text:
A DICOM directory can hold several series or several geometric stacks. read raises in that case; read_all returns all of them:

images, report = medvol.read_all("dicom_dir/")             # one Image per stack (dicom_stacks="split")
image, report = medvol.read("dicom_dir/", dicom_stacks="largest")

docs.title: Write
docs.text:
report = medvol.write(image, "ct.mla")      # the format comes from the extension
report = medvol.write(image, "ct.nrrd")
report = medvol.write(image, "out_dir/", format="dicom")

Before writing, MedVol compares the image with what the target format can store (its capabilities). What it cannot store is listed in the report as dropped, or raises LossError with on_loss="error":

medvol.write(image, "ct.mha", on_loss="error")

docs.title: Convert
docs.text:
convert is read followed by write; the report covers both steps.

report = medvol.convert("ct.mla", "ct.nrrd")
print(report)

convert mla -> nrrd ct.mla -> ct.nrrd
  choice: nrrd_space = left-posterior-superior
  choice: layout = encoding gzip, little endian
  warning: source header (nifti): its fields are not written to nrrd; only the core is converted (spec 6, 9)

The original NIfTI header travels inside the .mla and is used again only when the image is written back to NIfTI (see Geometry and metadata).

docs.title: Policies
docs.text:
Every ambiguity is resolved by a named policy. Pass them as keyword arguments, or as a reusable medvol.Policy:

image, report = medvol.read("ct.nii.gz", nifti_form="sform", world_frame="ras")

policy = medvol.Policy(dicom_tilt="exact", on_loss="error")
medvol.convert("dicom_dir/", "ct.nii.gz", policy=policy)
medvol.convert("dicom_dir/", "ct.nii.gz", policy=policy, dicom_stacks="largest")   # override one option

docs.title: Reorient
docs.text:
MedVol never reorients unless asked. reorient transposes and flips the array (never resamples) so that its space axes, fastest first, point closest to x, y, z of LPS or RAS. Every voxel keeps its world position, and axis names travel with their axes:

ras = medvol.reorient(image, "RAS")
image, report = medvol.read("ct.nii.gz", reorient="RAS")   # the same, while reading

docs.title: MLArray
docs.text:
Image and mlarray.MLArray convert into each other:

from mlarray import MLArray

array = image.to_mlarray(patch_size=(128, 128, 128))   # in-memory MLArray; layout options as for MLArray
array.save("ct.mla")
image = medvol.Image.from_mlarray(MLArray("ct.mla"))

medvol.write(image, "ct.mla") does the same with MLArray's default layout. MLArray's mlarray_convert command uses MedVol.

docs.title: DICOM
docs.text:
DICOM support needs pip install "medvol[dicom]".

  • Series (single-frame CT, MR, PET, ...): slices are grouped by series and geometry and sorted by their position along the slice normal, never by InstanceNumber. Tilted (gantry tilt) series get a sheared matrix (dicom_tilt="exact"), irregular spacing raises unless dicom_irregular_spacing says otherwise.
  • Enhanced multi-frame, including 4-D, with per-frame geometry.
  • Rescale: slope and intercept become values.scale / values.offset when every slice shares them. When they differ per slice (PET), reading fails unless dicom_rescale="apply", which stores the physical values as float.
  • Writing re-emits the original series from source, with the original UIDs. New DICOM image series from other formats are not created.
  • SEG files read as label maps with their segment names, colours and codes (values.labels); fractional SEGs read as probability maps. A label map (values.kind label or probability) is written as a DICOM SEG on its referenced image series:
seg, _ = medvol.read("labels.nii.gz")
seg.meta.values = {"kind": "label", "labels": {"1": {"name": "liver"}, "2": {"name": "tumor"}}}
medvol.write(seg, "seg.dcm", format="dicom", reference="ct_dir/")   # a directory, file list or datasets

NIfTI has no label table, so an image read from NIfTI is a measurement until you say otherwise, as above. - RTSTRUCT contours are rasterised onto the referenced series: read the RTSTRUCT together with its series (same directory), or pass reference="ct_dir/" to read.
